errors.scoring_consequence: A substitution error of this kind keeps the early points but blocks the final interval point (sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10014 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are algebra slips inside the substitution.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the ratio gives for a negative value of the variable; a student who reports a negative limit and still compares it with one is not distinguishing the two series, while one who restores the bars simplified them away.
errors.name: Ratio test carried out without absolute values
non_conceptual_causes: the bars dropped because every displayed term of the printed series is positive
the absolute value written on the first line and lost once the algebra was simplified
the ratio copied from a worked example whose terms were positive
errors.observed_behavior: The response forms and evaluates the ratio of consecutive terms without absolute value bars.
errors.scoring_consequence: A ratio without absolute values still earns the setup and limit points, but the interior point then requires the inequality to be resolved without error (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which series was tested and what its convergence implies about the other; a student who cannot state the implication holds the belief, while one who states it and then rereads the label transposed two words.
errors.name: Absolute and conditional convergence labels interchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the label written from the last test run rather than from the pair of findings
only one of the two series tested and the label chosen from that single result
the two labels transposed when the answer was copied to the final line
errors.observed_behavior: The response labels a series conditionally convergent when the absolute value series converges, or absolutely convergent when only the signed series converges.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification point is lost, since the two labels are exclusive.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which terms the partial sum contains and which term comes next; a student who names the next term correctly and still bounds with another term has a counting slip, while one who cannot say which term is omitted is applying the bound without its conditions.
errors.name: Bounding term taken from the wrong position in the series
non_conceptual_causes: the last index of the partial sum counted as the first omitted index
the sum read as ending at n when the sigma runs to n minus one
the bounding term taken from the term that was easiest to evaluate
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response bounds the error with a term already included in the partial sum, or with a term further along than the first omitted one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point is earned only for the correct omitted term, and a term of higher degree does not earn it (sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10017 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are counting slips in locating the first omitted term.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what value of the variable the approximation is being made at; a student who names it and still substitutes the index is not separating index from variable, while one who recomputes on the spot made a substitution slip.
errors.name: Bounding term evaluated at the wrong input
non_conceptual_causes: the index n substituted in place of the stated input
the centre of the series substituted because the term was read from the general form
a power of a negative input evaluated without parentheses
errors.observed_behavior: The response identifies the correct omitted term but substitutes the index, the centre, or another value in place of the stated input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point attached to using the term correctly is lost (sg-22:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the error is known exactly or only bounded and which symbol says so; a student who claims exact knowledge holds the belief, while one who names the inequality wrote the relation loosely.
errors.name: Error written as equal to the bounding term
non_conceptual_causes: the equals sign used to join the error and the bound as one line of work
the inequality symbol chosen after the value was computed and pointed the wrong way
the phrase at most in the prompt not carried into the written relation
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016, BC-ERR-99002.
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the error as equal to the bounding expression rather than at most that expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: A statement of equality does not earn the justification point in either bound (sg-22:21, sg-23:20, sg-24:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to finish the sentence stating what the error is less than; a student who supplies the tolerance at once omitted a line, while one who offers the bound as the answer is treating bound and error as one object.
errors.name: Comparison with the tolerance left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: the bounding value computed and the comparison sentence left unwritten
the tolerance read as the number to compute rather than the number to beat
the comparison carried out mentally with only the verdict recorded
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the bounding value but never states that it is at most the tolerance the prompt named.
errors.scoring_consequence: The communication point requires the inequality against the tolerance to be presented (sg-23:20, sg-22:21).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-99007 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are omissions in presenting the final comparison.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors being differentiated before writing anything; a student who names them and then still omits a factor made a rule omission, while one who does not see two factors misread the relation.
errors.name: Higher derivative computed without the product or chain rule
non_conceptual_causes: the product rule omitted on a product of two functions of x
the chain rule factor dropped when an inner function was differentiated
the higher derivative written in one step with no intermediate expression recorded
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99013.
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates a relation defining a derivative and omits a product rule factor or a chain rule factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form of the rule is scored separately from the resulting derivative, so an omitted factor loses the second point while the first may survive (sg-23:19).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10019 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are omissions of a differentiation rule.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the coefficient of the second degree term is when the second derivative at the centre is six; an answer of six points to the belief, while an answer of three followed by later omissions points to an inconsistent application.
errors.name: Taylor coefficient written without dividing by the factorial
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative value written straight into the coefficient slot
the factorial placed in the numerator instead of the denominator
the factorial included for the second degree term and omitted thereafter
errors.observed_behavior: The response places the derivative value directly as the coefficient of the power, with no factorial denominator.
errors.scoring_consequence: The polynomial is not the requested one and its term points are lost (sg-23:19).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what degree the requested polynomial has and which terms belong to it; a student who says the polynomial and the series are the same object holds the belief, while one who names the degree and strikes the extra terms copied from a neighbouring part.
errors.name: Polynomial presented with extra terms or a trailing ellipsis
non_conceptual_causes: the ellipsis carried over from a series written in an earlier part
the requested degree read as a number of terms
extra terms retained because the expansion was produced before the degree was checked
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes a polynomial that includes terms beyond the requested degree, or appends an ellipsis, turning the answer into a series.
errors.scoring_consequence: A polynomial with terms of higher degree, or with an ellipsis, does not earn the final polynomial point (sg-23:20, sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative belongs in the coefficient of the third degree term and why; a student who names the third derivative and still reads the wrong row made a table slip, while one who names a different order is not tying order to degree.
errors.name: Derivative values taken from the wrong row or order
non_conceptual_causes: a row of the table read one line off
the order of the derivative paired with the power by position in the table rather than by order
a value read from a column for a different centre
errors.observed_behavior: The response reads a table of derivative values and pairs a derivative of one order with the power of another.
errors.scoring_consequence: Each misplaced value spoils the term that depends on it.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-10019 is a plausible internal cause; the other routes are misreadings of the table layout.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative appears in the bound for a fourth degree polynomial; a student who names the fourth is off by one in the order, while one who names the fifth and still omits the maximum is assembling the bound from remembered fragments.
errors.name: Lagrange bound assembled in the wrong form
non_conceptual_causes: the power of x minus a written with n in place of n plus one
the factorial written as n factorial rather than n plus one factorial
the maximum of the next derivative replaced by its value at the centre
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the bound without the maximum of the next derivative, with the wrong power of the difference, or with the wrong factorial.
errors.scoring_consequence: The form point is lost, and with it the comparison point that depends on it (sg-23:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the series alternates and whether a bound on the next derivative is available; a student who answers both and keeps the wrong bound is applying a bound without its conditions, while one who switches had not inspected the series.
errors.name: Error bound chosen whose conditions the situation does not meet
non_conceptual_causes: the bound chosen from the shape of the prompt rather than from the series in hand
the alternating factor not noticed in the series at the given input
a derivative bound supplied in the stem read as an instruction to use the Lagrange form
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99016.
errors.observed_behavior: The response reaches for the Lagrange bound where the alternating series bound is the available tool, or the reverse, without checking the conditions.
errors.scoring_consequence: A bound whose conditions are not met earns no justification point (sg-24:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the first two terms of the series at that endpoint; a student who produces terms still containing the variable substituted into the wrong slot, while one who produces numbers and reuses the other endpoint's verdict is treating the two ends alike.
errors.name: Endpoint value substituted into the wrong place in the general term
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoint substituted for the index n rather than for the variable
the alternating factor produced by a negative endpoint cancelled against an existing sign
the endpoint substituted into the displayed terms but not into the general term
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the endpoint for the index rather than for the variable, or drops the alternating factor produced by a negative endpoint.
errors.scoring_consequence: The endpoint series is wrong, so the analysis and interval points are lost (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the two inequalities that the absolute value statement stands for.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped when the ratio inequality is solved
non_conceptual_causes: algebra slip
time pressure
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response converts the inequality on the ratio into a one sided inequality, producing a half interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: An inequality in absolute value alone is not sufficient for the interior point; the compound inequality is required (sg-22:21, sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how far the interval reaches from its centre; a student who says the interval is the radius holds the conflation, while one who halves the width at once answered the previous part's question.
errors.name: Interval presented where the radius of convergence was requested
non_conceptual_causes: the word radius in the prompt read as interval
the last expression produced by the algebra copied onto the answer line
the half-length never computed because the interval was the object of the previous part
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the inequality and presents an interval without naming the radius as a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The radius point cannot be earned by presenting an interval alone (sg-21:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the series becomes at each end of the interval; a student who says the ratio test already settled the ends holds the belief, while one who writes both endpoint series unprompted stopped early.
errors.name: Endpoints of the interval left untested
non_conceptual_causes: the ratio test finished and the part left when time ran short
the endpoints named and the two series never written out
the open interval copied from the inequality straight to the answer line
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99017.
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the open interval found from the ratio test as the interval of convergence without examining either endpoint.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the endpoint consideration point and the interval point are lost (sg-25:24).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which endpoints belong to the interval and how the notation shows that; a student whose spoken answer matches the tests but not the brackets has a notation slip, while one who reports both ends alike is treating the two endpoints as a single case.
errors.name: Interval reported with endpoint inclusion that contradicts the endpoint analysis
non_conceptual_causes: a square bracket written beside the infinity symbol
the brackets written before the endpoint tests were finished
the endpoint findings recorded in scratch work and never transferred to the interval
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99037.
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests the endpoints correctly and then writes an interval whose brackets do not match the findings, or attaches a closed bracket to an unbounded end.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final interval point requires the interval to match the analysis (sg-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to substitute n equal to one and two into the proposed general term.
errors.name: General term of a series mis-differentiated or mis-assembled
non_conceptual_causes: algebra slip in the exponent
off by one slip in the index
time pressure
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99018.
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes several correct terms but produces a general term that does not reproduce them, often after differentiating with respect to the index or mishandling the alternating factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The general term is a separate scored point from the first terms (sg-25:26, sg-24:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the first three terms of the cosine series and of the exponential series separately; a student who gives the same sign pattern for both has merged two memorised lists, while one who separates them and still drops factorials has a recall gap in the coefficients.
errors.name: Standard Maclaurin series recalled incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the alternating factor of the cosine series attached to the exponential series
even powers written where odd powers belong in the sine series
the factorial denominators omitted, so the expansion reduces to a geometric form
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the series for the exponential, the sine, the cosine, or one over one minus x with wrong signs, wrong parities of the powers, or missing factorials.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every term built on the misremembered series is wrong, so the dependent points are lost (sg-23:21).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second term becomes when the substitution is written with parentheses; a student who then corrects the whole expansion lost parentheses, while one who also relocates the centre holds a belief about what substitution does.
errors.name: Substitution into a known series carried out incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the substituted expression not enclosed in parentheses before being raised to the power
a constant factor applied to the first term only
the substitution made in the displayed terms and not in the general term
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99009.
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes an expression for the variable in a known series but does not raise the whole expression to the required power, or loses a constant factor.
errors.scoring_consequence: The resulting series is wrong from the first affected term onward.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the radius under term-by-term differentiation before any computation; a student who says it may change holds the belief, while one who states that it is unchanged and still reports a different value made an algebra slip in the rerun.
errors.name: Radius of a differentiated or integrated series recomputed or claimed to change
non_conceptual_causes: the ratio test rerun on the derived series with an algebra slip in the exponent
the derived series treated as unconnected to the series it came from
the radius recomputed because the part was read as asking for a fresh interval
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts a different radius for the derived series, or redoes the ratio test and reports a value inconsistent with the original radius.
errors.scoring_consequence: The radius point rests on the preservation statement, so an inconsistent value loses it (sg-24:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the input sits relative to the interval found earlier; a student who says the series represents the function at every input holds the belief, while one who locates the input correctly omitted the reason under time pressure.
errors.name: Convergence at a specified input asserted without a reason
non_conceptual_causes: the input compared with the centre rather than with the ends of the interval
the verdict written because the input appeared in an earlier part of the stem
the interval found earlier in the question not carried into the final part
errors.notes: Matches the cross-unit Chief Reader error record BC-ERR-99001.
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the series does or does not converge at the given input without placing the input relative to the interval of convergence.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point requires the position relative to the interval to be given (sg-25:27).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same function on an interval of length one and then on an interval of length four and ask for both averages.
errors.name: Average value reported without dividing by the interval length
non_conceptual_causes: the divisor was written in the setup and dropped when the value was transcribed
the interval length was computed as the sum of the endpoints rather than their difference
the response stopped after the integral was evaluated when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The response presents the correct definite integral and reports its value as the average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The average value point is lost unless the correct answer appears elsewhere as evidence of the division (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the interval in the prompt before writing the quotient.
errors.name: Average taken over an interval the question did not name
non_conceptual_causes: the interval endpoints in the stem were read as the endpoints of the graph window
the limits were copied from the previous part of the same question
the table column for the stated interval was read one row off
errors.observed_behavior: The limits of the average value integral, or the divisor, come from an interval other than the one the prompt states.
errors.scoring_consequence: Both the setup point and the answer point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the integral of a rate that is negative on the whole interval.
errors.name: Region below the axis counted as positive area in an average
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
misread of the prompt
errors.observed_behavior: A graph dipping below the axis contributes a positive amount to the integral used in the average.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is wrong, so the answer point is lost while the formula point may stand.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the student entered into the calculator, written as an integral.
errors.name: Calculator answer presented with no setup
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a belief that the work is scratch
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears with no integral and no evidence of the division.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost; an unsupported value can still earn an answer point only where the guideline says so (sg-25:3).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same computation with the unrounded stored value and compare.
errors.name: Intermediate value rounded before the final computation
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A stored decimal is truncated to two or three places and then used in a later step, moving the reported answer.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for inappropriate rounding, and at most one point per question is withheld on this ground (sg-25:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Show both expressions side by side and ask for the units of each.
errors.name: Average value computed where an average rate of change was asked, or the reverse
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the prompt
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response builds a difference quotient when the average of the function values was requested, or an integral quotient when the average rate of change was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned, because the quantity is not the one asked for (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the units of the integrand and of the differential separately and then multiply them.
errors.name: Units omitted or built from the wrong factors
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
misread of the prompt
errors.observed_behavior: A reported value carries no units, or units that are the rate units rather than the rate units multiplied by the input units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point, where one exists, is lost; in 2025 the units for an average rate of change were scored as their own point (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a velocity that is positive then negative and ask for both quantities in the same part.
errors.name: Displacement reported where total distance was asked
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the prompt
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates velocity without the absolute value and reports the result as the distance travelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand is wrong, and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the speed of a particle whose velocity is negative at that instant.
errors.name: Speed written without the absolute value or the magnitude
non_conceptual_causes: the absolute value bars were written in the setup and lost when the integral was keyed in
a template from a displacement exercise was copied unchanged
a negative sign was dropped while a constant was distributed through the velocity expression
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand for total distance is the velocity itself rather than its absolute value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the integral on each side of the zero of velocity before the total is requested.
errors.name: Interval not split where velocity changes sign
non_conceptual_causes: the zero of velocity was found in an earlier part and not carried forward
one integral was keyed in to save time near the end of the section
the calculator window hid the crossing of the horizontal axis
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates velocity over the whole interval and takes one absolute value at the end.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is too small, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give the same rate with two different starting amounts and ask for the later value in each case.
errors.name: Initial value not added to the accumulated change
non_conceptual_causes: the initial amount in the stem was read as the amount at the end of the interval
the addition was done mentally and the sum was never written
the response stopped after the integral when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the integral of the rate and reports it as the value of the quantity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number would be if the starting amount were doubled.
errors.name: Net change reported as the amount present
non_conceptual_causes: the phrase asking how much is present was read as asking how much it changed
the initial condition appeared in an earlier part and was not carried into this one
errors.observed_behavior: A question asking how much is present at a time is answered with the net change over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost even when the integral is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the net rate should be at a time when the two rates are equal.
errors.name: Inflow and outflow rates added instead of subtracted
non_conceptual_causes: the two rate names in the stem were assigned to the wrong roles
a minus sign was dropped while the two rate expressions were combined
the second rate was copied from the wrong table column
errors.observed_behavior: The net rate is written as the sum of the two rates, or the difference is taken in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say which terms the minus sign reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost when a supplied expression is placed in an integrand
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A subtracted rate or a difference is substituted without parentheses, so only its first term is affected by the operation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is wrong, so the setup point is lost; the Chief Reader records this behaviour across questions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the value at the endpoint has been compared with the value at the critical point.
errors.name: Local argument offered for an absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that an accumulated amount is largest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the amount at both ends of the interval.
errors.name: Endpoints omitted from a candidates table
non_conceptual_causes: the candidates table was started and left unfinished when time ran out
the endpoint values were computed on the calculator and never transcribed
errors.observed_behavior: The candidates test evaluates the amount only at the interior critical point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is not global (sg-25:5).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the limits were different.
errors.name: Interpretation names the quantity but not the interval
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence was written before the limits were substituted and never revised
the interval was stated in an earlier part and treated as already said
errors.observed_behavior: The sentence says what is accumulating without saying between which inputs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost because the guideline requires the interval as well as the quantity (sg-23:2).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the variable of integration in the expression as written.
errors.name: Differential omitted from an integral expression
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
arithmetic slip
errors.observed_behavior: An integral is written with limits and an integrand but no dx, dt, or dy.
errors.scoring_consequence: Whether the point survives depends on the guideline; in 2023 a missing differential kept the setup point but could block the answer point when the expression was also equated to a value (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two inputs bound the region and why.
errors.name: Limits of integration taken from the wrong inputs
non_conceptual_causes: the intersection abscissas were solved for and the ordinates were copied instead
the calculator window settings were used as the endpoints
one of the two intersection values was transcribed with a sign error
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is set up with limits that are not the boundary of the region or the interval requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, and in 2023 incorrect limits also made a response ineligible for the final area point (sg-23:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate both functions at one interior input and say which is larger.
errors.name: Difference of the boundary functions taken in the wrong order
non_conceptual_causes: the two function labels in the stem were exchanged when the integrand was written
the order was copied from an earlier exercise in which the roles were reversed
a minus sign was dropped while the second function was distributed
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the lower curve minus the upper curve, or the left curve minus the right curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point may survive, since either order earned it in 2023, but a negative value reported as an area loses the answer point (sg-23:16, sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the statement by evaluating both sides.
errors.name: Area asserted to equal an expression that is its negative
non_conceptual_causes: the reversed difference was written first and the sign was corrected only in the final value
the expression was transcribed from scratch work in which the order was right
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the reversed difference, sets it equal to the positive area, and reports the positive value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for the incorrect statement even though the reported number is right (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the lower limit becomes after the substitution and why.
errors.name: Limits kept in the old variable after a substitution
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: An antiderivative found by substitution is evaluated at the original limits without converting them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response is not eligible for the answer point (sg-23:17).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the variable of integration and to check that the integrand contains only that variable.
errors.name: Integrand written in one variable with the differential of another
non_conceptual_causes: the differential was changed to match the limits without rewriting the integrand
the curve was not solved for the other variable because the algebra stalled
the setup was copied from a part that integrated in the other variable
errors.observed_behavior: A function of x is integrated with respect to y, or the reverse, without being rewritten.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the expression does not define a number.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the smallest and largest y value in the region.
errors.name: Limits given as values of the variable not being integrated
non_conceptual_causes: the intersection point was found and its x coordinate was copied in place of its y coordinate
the limits were carried over unchanged from the previous part
errors.observed_behavior: An integral in y carries x values as its limits.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost and the value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many solutions the equation of the two curves has on the interval.
errors.name: An interior intersection point not found
non_conceptual_causes: the calculator window showed only part of the interval
the solver returned one root and was not run again from a second guess
the third crossing was visible on the figure but was never marked
errors.observed_behavior: Only the outer two crossings are used, so an interior crossing is integrated across.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because part of the region is subtracted rather than added.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the integrand on each side of the crossing.
errors.name: One integral used across a crossing of the curves
non_conceptual_causes: the split was planned in scratch work and only one integral was keyed in
the second integral was left unwritten when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: A fixed order of subtraction is integrated over an interval in which the curves exchange places.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported area is smaller than the true area and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integral would give if the two lobes had equal area.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped from a split region integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the bars were written in the setup and lost when the expression was keyed in
a single integral form was copied from a note without its bars
errors.observed_behavior: The single integral form is written without the absolute value bars around the difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value returned is the signed difference of the lobes, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark the slice on the figure and label both of its ends.
errors.name: Cross sectional side written as one function value
non_conceptual_causes: the lower boundary in the stem was read as the horizontal axis
the slice was drawn on the figure with only its upper end labelled
errors.observed_behavior: The side of the slice is taken as the upper curve alone although the region is bounded by two curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is wrong, so the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which shape the area formula in the integrand describes.
errors.name: Factor of pi placed in a polygonal cross section integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the integrand was copied from a disc exercise
the shape named in the stem was read as circular
errors.observed_behavior: A square or triangular cross section volume carries a factor of pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand belongs to the wrong volume family.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand both expressions for a specific pair of numbers and compare.
errors.name: Square of a difference used where a difference of squares is needed
non_conceptual_causes: the two radius expressions were subtracted before being squared during transcription
a sign was dropped while the squared binomial was expanded
errors.observed_behavior: A washer integrand is written as the square of the difference of the two radii, or a squared difference is expanded term by term.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost, and the value is wrong by the cross term.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one slice with both dimensions labelled.
errors.name: Second dimension of a rectangular cross section omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the stated multiple relating height to base was skipped when the stem was read
the factor was written in the setup and lost when the integral was keyed in
errors.observed_behavior: A rectangular section whose height is a stated multiple of its base is treated as a square.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a single slice of the named shape with a numerical side.
errors.name: Constant factor of a cross sectional area formula wrong or missing
non_conceptual_causes: the fractional constant was written in the setup and dropped when the integral was keyed in
the constant was recalled for a different named shape
errors.observed_behavior: The area of an equilateral or semicircular section is written without its fractional constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which side of the triangle lies in the base region.
errors.name: Distance between the curves used as a leg when it is the hypotenuse
non_conceptual_causes: the word naming which side lies in the base region was skipped when the stem was read
the figure was marked with the distance along the wrong side of the triangle
errors.observed_behavior: A right isosceles section is given the leg formula although the stated distance is the hypotenuse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand is off by a factor of two, so the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the radius of a semicircle whose diameter is a stated length.
errors.name: Distance between the curves used as the radius of a semicircle
non_conceptual_causes: the halving was done in scratch work and not carried into the integrand
the word diameter in the stem was read as radius
errors.observed_behavior: The semicircular section is given a radius equal to the whole distance between the boundary curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The volume is four times too large and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a semicircle of a stated radius.
errors.name: Full circle area used for a semicircular cross section
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The area formula omits the factor of one half that makes the section a semicircle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The volume is twice the correct value and the setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of one disc of a stated radius.
errors.name: Radius left unsquared in a solid of revolution integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the integrand was keyed in
the setup was copied from an area between curves exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The disc integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times the square of the function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the area of a circular slice of that radius is.
errors.name: Factor of pi omitted from a solid of revolution integrand
non_conceptual_causes: the factor pi was written outside the integral in scratch work and not carried to the answer line
the constant was left for a final multiplication that time ran out before
errors.observed_behavior: A disc or washer volume is reported without the constant factor pi.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the distance from a point on the curve to the stated line.
errors.name: Radius measured from a coordinate axis when the axis of revolution is elsewhere
non_conceptual_causes: the line of revolution in the stem was read as a coordinate axis
the subtraction was set up on the figure and not carried into the integrand
errors.observed_behavior: The response revolves about a line other than an axis but writes the radius as the bare function value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which inputs the region occupies, independently of where the axis is.
errors.name: Limits of integration moved along with the axis of revolution
non_conceptual_causes: the translation applied to the radius was applied a second time to the endpoints
the endpoints were copied from scratch work in which the shift had already been made
errors.observed_behavior: The interval of integration is translated by the same amount as the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost and the value is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the axis at one interior input.
errors.name: Outer and inner radii of a washer exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the two curve labels were exchanged when the integrand was written
the distances to the axis were compared at an input outside the region
errors.observed_behavior: The nearer curve is used as the outer radius, giving a negative integrand.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative volume is reported and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the length of a straight segment of slope one on an interval of length one should be.
errors.name: Arc length integrand written without the radical or without the added one
non_conceptual_causes: the radical was written in scratch work and the answer line was copied from an earlier step
the formula was recalled from a note in which the added one had been omitted
errors.observed_behavior: The length integral is written as the integral of the derivative, or of the square root of the derivative squared alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the integrand for a linear function and compare with the Pythagorean length.
errors.name: Derivative not squared inside the arc length radical
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the radical was keyed into the calculator
the square was written outside the radical and then cancelled during simplification
the derivative was substituted into a formula copied with the square already removed
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the square root of one plus the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-08024 is a plausible internal cause here, since the structure of the radical is the single idea at issue; the non-conceptual causes carry the alternatives.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the limits of the integral tell about the piece of curve being measured.
errors.name: Arc length identified without naming the interval
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence was written before the limits were substituted and never revised
the interval was named in an earlier part and treated as already said
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the integral gives the length of the curve but does not say on which interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval point is lost while the arc length point stands (sg-24:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the integrand would be if the area under the graph were wanted.
errors.name: Arc length integral described as an area
non_conceptual_causes: the word length in the stem was read as area
the interpretation sentence was copied from an area between curves part of the same question
errors.observed_behavior: The displayed radical integral is interpreted as the area under the graph.
errors.scoring_consequence: The identification point is lost (sg-24:16).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical length or volume reported with no integral shown
non_conceptual_causes: the expression was kept on the calculator screen and never transcribed
the answer line was written last with the setup left in scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for an arc length or a volume with no integral expression anywhere in the response.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which conditions the theorem requires before the conclusion may be drawn.
errors.name: Theorem hypotheses not stated before the conclusion is used
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
misread of the question or the figure
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the Mean Value Theorem or the Extreme Value Theorem and never mentions continuity or differentiability on the stated interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost even when the conclusion is correct, because the guideline makes the continuity statement a condition of that point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the function is continuous on the closed interval: an answer that the theorem's name is enough is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, an answer that the conclusion may be used regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, and a correct spoken answer with the sentence missing only on paper is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Continuity not drawn from the given differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: the continuity sentence is written on scratch work and never transferred to the response
the stem's phrase differentiable on the closed interval is skimmed and read as already continuous
the part is reached late and the hypothesis sentence is the first thing cut
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that the function is continuous without saying that differentiability supplies it, or omits continuity altogether.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point tied to the hypothesis is lost; the 2025 guideline refused a bare statement that the function is continuous.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the quotient written symbolically before any numbers are substituted: averaging the two endpoint values is consistent with BC-MIS-05003, an integral divided by the interval length is consistent with BC-MIS-99006, and a correct symbolic form carrying a wrong number is consistent with the column and keying causes.
errors.name: Average rate of change formed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the two endpoint values are read from the wrong table columns
the subtraction is keyed into the calculator in the reversed order
the denominator is taken as one endpoint rather than the difference of the endpoints
errors.observed_behavior: The response averages the two endpoint values, reverses the order of subtraction, or divides by the wrong difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the average rate of change is lost and any solved value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state the conclusion in one sentence: naming the theorem but not the claim is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, asserting the claim with no theorem is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, and producing both fluently on request is consistent with the transfer and misreading causes.
errors.name: Existence asserted with no affirmative answer or no theorem
non_conceptual_causes: the affirmative sentence is spoken while working and never written
the theorem name is left on scratch work with the arithmetic
the stem is read as a computation because the previous part asked for one
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the needed arithmetic but never says yes and never names a theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the guideline requires an affirmative answer in some form.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the reported input lies strictly between the endpoints: treating the open interval as an optional detail is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, treating any solution of the equation as the theorem's output is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, and discarding the stray root once asked is consistent with the root selection and misreading causes.
errors.name: Solved value reported outside the open interval
non_conceptual_causes: the second root of a quadratic is kept without testing it against the interval
the interval endpoints are misread from the stem
the value is reported straight from the calculator solver with no domain check
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the derivative equation and reports a solution that is an endpoint or lies outside the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the theorem places the point strictly inside the interval.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which theorem concerns values of the function and which concerns values of the derivative: one theorem offered for both kinds of claim is consistent with BC-MIS-05005, a name supplied as the whole justification is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, and a correct distinction with the wrong name on paper is consistent with the copying and misreading causes.
errors.name: Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the theorem is chosen because it is the one most recently practised
the stem's symbol for the derivative value is read as a function value
the theorem name is copied from a neighbouring part of the same question
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies the existence of an input with a given derivative value by appealing to the Intermediate Value Theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline names this as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens on the same interval for a function with a jump in the middle: an answer that the extrema still exist is consistent with BC-MIS-05006, an answer that the hypotheses need not be established is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, and spotting the jump at once is consistent with the misreading and transfer causes.
errors.name: Extreme Value Theorem invoked without continuity on the closed interval
non_conceptual_causes: the break in the piecewise definition is not noticed in the stem
the interval is copied as closed where the stem wrote it open
the hypothesis is checked on the graph and never written down
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims that a maximum and a minimum are attained for a function with a break inside the interval, or on an open interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost and the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the theorem tells you and what it does not: claiming it names the input is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, offering the name in place of the argument is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, and separating existence from location on request is consistent with the misreading and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Existence theorem used to locate the extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the question's word where is read as whether
the extremum located in an earlier part is carried into this one
the theorem is recalled from a worked example that also located the extremum
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the Extreme Value Theorem as though it named the input at which the extremum occurs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response answers a different question and the location it reports is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what equation produced the listed inputs: an answer that any listed input is automatically an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the list is itself the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and reciting the equation immediately is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Zeros of the derivative listed without stating the derivative condition
non_conceptual_causes: the equation is solved on the calculator and only the roots are copied
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
the part is written last and only the answer line is filled
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes down the inputs at which the derivative vanishes but never presents the equation setting the derivative equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point of the candidates test is lost; the 2023 guideline states that listing the zeros is not sufficient.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input: keeping it as a critical point regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, treating the domain gap as not interrupting the behaviour is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, and dropping it once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and calculator causes.
errors.name: Solutions outside the domain retained as critical points
non_conceptual_causes: a factor is cancelled from the derivative although it also vanishes in the denominator
the domain of the original function is never written down
the root comes from a calculator zero with no check that the function has a value there
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input at which the derivative expression vanishes although the function itself is undefined there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The candidate list is wrong and the comparison that follows cannot be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark every input where the derivative graph breaks: an answer that only zeros count is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the derivative exists wherever the function does is consistent with BC-MIS-05009, and marking the corner correctly on request is consistent with the simplification and scale causes.
errors.name: Inputs where the derivative fails to exist omitted from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative is read from a simplified formula that hides the corner
the sharp point on the figure reads as a smooth turn at the plotted scale
only the roots the solver returned are listed
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds only the zeros of the derivative and skips corners, cusps, and vertical tangents.
errors.scoring_consequence: A candidate is missing, so the comparison may select the wrong extremum and the justification is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether any other input could give a larger value: an answer that a local high point is the highest is consistent with BC-MIS-05007, an answer that the local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and completing the comparison on request is consistent with the endpoint and timing causes.
errors.name: Relative extremum reported as the absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoint values are never evaluated
the word absolute in the stem is skimmed
the comparison table is begun and abandoned when the part runs out of time
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds a local high or low point and reports it as the largest or smallest value on the interval without comparing the rest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is local where a global claim was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative immediately on each side: an answer that every critical point is an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, a classification drawn from the size of the derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and reporting the same sign twice once asked is consistent with the test point and multiplicity causes.
errors.name: Critical point with no sign change declared an extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the sign of the derivative is tested on one side of the input only
the test point chosen on one side lies beyond the next critical point
a factor of even multiplicity is charted as a sign change
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum or minimum at an input where the derivative is zero but keeps its sign on both sides.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the derivative at one input inside the disputed interval: reading the derivative's sign from the function's sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, reading it from the second derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and a corrected sign on recomputation is consistent with the substitution and test point causes.
errors.name: Sign of the derivative misread on an interval
non_conceptual_causes: a test value is substituted into the function rather than into the derivative
the sign of a negative factor is dropped while multiplying the factors in the chart
the test point falls outside the interval it was meant to represent
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the derivative expression on one of the intervals of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported intervals are wrong, which also forfeits the reason point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the plotted curve and the function under discussion separately before answering: treating the drawn curve as the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, treating the derivative as fixing the function outright is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, and labelling both correctly on request is consistent with the axis label and transcription causes.
errors.name: Plotted derivative read as the function itself
non_conceptual_causes: the axis label on the figure is not read
the figure is carried over from a previous part where the function itself was plotted
the curve is labelled correctly on scratch work and the answer sentence names the wrong object
errors.observed_behavior: The response answers a question about the function by describing features of the curve shown, which is the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every part that rests on the plotted object is answered about the wrong function.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a curve that is decreasing and concave up at once: an answer that no such curve exists is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, an answer that the second derivative behaves like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and drawing it correctly while the written answer still swaps the two is consistent with the referent and ordering causes.
errors.name: Increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the word increasing in the stem is attached to the plotted curve rather than to the function
the sign chart is built from the plotted curve's values instead of its slopes
the two questions inside the part are answered in the reverse order
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concavity where monotonicity was asked for, or reports increase of the function where the derivative graph is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported belong to the other question and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the domain of the function before the sign chart is drawn: an answer that a gap does not interrupt an interval is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, an answer that the derivative's sign follows the function's sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, and adding the missing partition point once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and window causes.
errors.name: Sign chart omits a point where the function is undefined
non_conceptual_causes: the denominator is cancelled before the partition points are collected
the domain is never written down before the chart is drawn
the asymptote lies outside the calculator window that was used
errors.observed_behavior: The response partitions the number line at the zeros of the derivative only and ignores a vertical asymptote or a domain gap.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interval spans a break, so the reported behaviour is claimed where the function does not exist.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite the sentence with every pronoun replaced by a name: restating the conclusion as the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, treating the presence of symbols as completing the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the object correctly at once is consistent with the carry-over and timing causes.
errors.name: Justification uses an unnamed referent
non_conceptual_causes: the pronoun is carried over from the stem's own wording
the sentence is written at speed at the end of the part
the object is named once in an earlier part and treated as still named
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the function or the graph changes sign, without naming which object is meant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the 2025 guideline names an ambiguous referent as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the input between the two stretches: merging them anyway is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, arguing from the function's own sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, and separating them on request is consistent with the transcription and window causes.
errors.name: Interval of increase reported across a gap in the domain
non_conceptual_causes: the two intervals are merged when the answer is copied from the sign chart
the undefined input lies outside the calculator window that was used
the union symbol is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The response merges two intervals of increase into one although the function is undefined between them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval reported is wrong and the reason point falls with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where a relative extremum is allowed to occur: an answer that any critical point qualifies is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the candidate list is the critical points only is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, and naming the rule correctly while the written work still samples is consistent with the table and solving causes.
errors.name: Candidate extrema sought away from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: inputs are sampled from a table supplied for a different part
the interval is scanned by substitution because the derivative looks hard to solve
the word relative in the stem is read as absolute, so endpoints are tested as well
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests inputs that are neither critical points nor endpoints when hunting for a relative extremum.
errors.scoring_consequence: Time is spent on inputs that cannot be extrema, and in a candidates argument extra inputs cost the justification point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the curve implied by their own sign statement: classifying from the derivative's value rather than its change is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, expecting the second derivative test to settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, and a sketch that contradicts the written answer is consistent with the reading direction and transposition causes.
errors.name: Direction of the sign change reversed in the classification
non_conceptual_causes: the sign chart is read right to left
the plus and minus labels are transposed when the chart is copied
the classification is carried over from a second derivative test done in an earlier part
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum where the derivative changes from negative to positive, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative on each side, not its size: classifying by magnitude is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, treating every critical point as an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, and giving the signs correctly once asked is consistent with the calculator table and skipped chart causes.
errors.name: Classification taken from the value of the derivative rather than its change
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative values at the two test points are compared in size rather than in sign
the test points are read from a calculator table showing magnitudes only
the sign chart is skipped because the derivative looks monotone
errors.observed_behavior: The response classifies the critical point by whether the derivative is large or small nearby instead of by its sign change.

errors.scoring_consequence: The quotient presented by itself is not sufficient for the answer point (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity was divided by what in the computation, and what unit that division produces.
errors.name: Units omitted or given as the units of the quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the units are copied from the table header, which records the quantity rather than its rate
the units are written on scratch work and not transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports an estimated derivative with no units, or with the units of the modelled quantity rather than of its rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is lost; it is earned for the correct compound units whether or not they are attached to a value, and an equivalent compound form is accepted (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two inputs the question names and have the student point to those rows before computing.
errors.name: Rows used that do not match the requested interval
non_conceptual_causes: an adjacent pair of rows is used because the named rows are further apart in the table
the interval endpoints in the stem are read from the wrong column
errors.observed_behavior: The response estimates the derivative from a pair of tabulated inputs other than the pair the question names or the pair that brackets the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the supporting work does not use the values the question specifies.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the denominator equals after the substitution, and whether that division is permitted.
errors.name: Increment set to zero before the common factor is divided out
non_conceptual_causes: the common factor is cancelled on scratch work and the uncancelled line is the one carried forward
the substitution is made on the first line because the expression is short
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes zero for the increment while it is still in the denominator.
errors.scoring_consequence: The simplification point and the value point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether each written line is a true equation on its own, and what the middle lines claim without the symbol.
errors.name: Limit symbol dropped during the computation
non_conceptual_causes: the shorthand used on a class board omits the symbol on intermediate lines
the limit symbol is written once at the top of a column of work and not repeated
errors.observed_behavior: The response manipulates the difference quotient without carrying the limit symbol and attaches it only to the final line.
errors.scoring_consequence: A notation point is lost where the definition itself is being assessed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate the shifted expression at one numerical increment both ways and compare the two numbers.
errors.name: Shifted term expanded incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the shifted argument is expanded the way a coefficient would distribute
a term is lost while the expanded square is copied to the next line
errors.observed_behavior: The response expands the function evaluated at the shifted input as though the function distributed over the sum.
errors.scoring_consequence: The simplification point and the value point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the increment appears in the written work, and whether a limit was taken anywhere.
errors.name: Derivative produced by rule where the definition was demanded
non_conceptual_causes: the instruction naming the definition is read after the work is already under way
the rule based answer is copied from scratch work onto a line headed by the definition
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates with the power rule and presents the result as an application of the definition.
errors.scoring_consequence: The points attached to the difference quotient and its simplification are lost although the final value may be right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name a function and a base point for which the expression is the difference quotient.
errors.name: Limit in derivative form reported as nonexistent
non_conceptual_causes: the expression is scanned for a factorable form only and the difference quotient shape is not tested
the base point is buried inside the expression and is not identified before the algebra starts
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats a limit having the shape of a difference quotient as indeterminate and unresolvable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which input makes the numerator vanish, and compare it with the input used in the evaluation.
errors.name: Wrong base point identified in a limit read as a derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the constant inside the function argument is read as the base point
the base point is identified correctly and then the wrong input is substituted while copying
errors.observed_behavior: The response identifies the underlying function correctly but evaluates its derivative at the wrong input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask on what grounds the function is continuous here, and whether that ground is stated in the response.
errors.name: Continuity asserted with no basis in an argument about a differentiable function
non_conceptual_causes: the clause naming the reason is dropped when the sentence is shortened
the reason is written in the margin and not in the argument
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the function is continuous without saying that it is continuous because it is differentiable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The continuity point requires the reason; a bare statement that the function is continuous does not earn it (sg-25:12).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a function that is continuous at a point but has no derivative there.
errors.name: Implication run backwards from continuity to differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: the implication is copied from notes with its two sides exchanged
the conclusion is written first and the hypothesis is filled in afterwards
errors.observed_behavior: The response concludes that a function is differentiable at a point because it is continuous there.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point is lost because the claim is not supported by the theorem.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope just left and just right of the point, and whether the two values agree.
errors.name: Non-differentiability claimed from the appearance of the graph alone
non_conceptual_causes: the one sided slopes are computed on scratch work and the written sentence keeps only the visual claim
the figure is drawn at a scale where a smooth turn looks sharp
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the derivative does not exist because the graph looks sharp, without reference to the one sided slopes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost although the verdict may be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope of a vertical line is.
errors.name: Vertical tangent treated as a horizontal one
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the graph
confusing the two tangent orientations
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the derivative at a vertical tangent as zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verdict point is lost because a value is reported where none exists.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to differentiate a squared term from the limit definition and compare the result with the rule.
errors.name: Exponent reduced without multiplying by it
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent is reduced first and the multiplying factor is never written in
the original exponent is copied incorrectly, so the factor that should appear is one
errors.observed_behavior: The response lowers the exponent by one but omits the factor of the original exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the graph of the constant term alone looks like and what its slope is.
errors.name: Constant term differentiated to itself
non_conceptual_causes: the constant term is copied along with the rest of the expression before differentiation begins
the constant sits at the end of a long expression and is transcribed without being processed
errors.observed_behavior: The response carries a constant term unchanged into the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite every term as a power before differentiating, and then to check that each term changed.
errors.name: Radical or reciprocal left undifferentiated
non_conceptual_causes: the radical term is not rewritten as a power, so no rule seems to apply to it
the term is copied to the answer line while the polynomial terms are being differentiated
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the polynomial terms and copies a radical or reciprocal term unchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope of the cosine graph is just to the right of the origin, and whether it is positive or negative.
errors.name: Sign dropped from the derivative of cosine
non_conceptual_causes: the sign is dropped while the derivative is copied from a memory aid
the pair of derivatives is recalled as one line and the sign is attached to the wrong member
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives sine as the derivative of cosine without the negative sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the expression carries the variable, the base or the exponent.
errors.name: Exponential differentiated by the power rule
non_conceptual_causes: the expression looks like a power because the variable sits in the exponent position
the base and the exponent are exchanged while the term is copied
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the natural exponential as a power of the variable and reduces its exponent.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to expand a short product first, differentiate the expansion, and compare with the reported answer.
errors.name: Product differentiated as a product of derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: the sum rule pattern from the preceding line is carried into the product
only one of the two product rule terms is transcribed from the scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: The response multiplies the derivatives of the two factors together.
errors.scoring_consequence: The rule point and the result point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to apply the rule to a quotient whose value is known and check the sign of the result.
errors.name: Quotient rule numerator terms reversed
non_conceptual_causes: the two numerator terms are written in the order the factors appear in the expression
the subtraction sign is placed after the terms are written and lands between the wrong pair
errors.observed_behavior: The response subtracts in the opposite order in the numerator of the quotient rule.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost because the derivative carries the wrong sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the units or the degree of the reported derivative are, and compare them with the degree the quotient should give.
errors.name: Denominator square omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the square is written on scratch work and is lost in the transcription
the denominator is long, so it is copied once without its exponent
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the quotient rule with the denominator rather than its square below the line.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the denominator changes when the variable changes.
errors.name: Quotient rule applied where the denominator is constant
non_conceptual_causes: the fraction bar in the expression triggers the rule before the denominator is read
the constant denominator is read as containing the variable because of a nearby symbol
errors.observed_behavior: The response applies the full quotient rule to an expression whose denominator carries no variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: No point is necessarily lost but the additional algebra invites a further error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label each substituted number with the symbol it stands for before the rule is applied.
errors.name: Function value used where a derivative value was required
non_conceptual_causes: the function column and the derivative column of the table are adjacent and the wrong one is read
the four required values are copied in one pass and two of them are swapped
errors.observed_behavior: The response substitutes the value of a function into a position in the product or quotient rule that calls for the value of its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to derive the derivative from the sine and cosine form and check where the negative sign arises.
errors.name: Cofunction derivative given without its negative sign
non_conceptual_causes: the sign is dropped when the result is copied from the quotient rule work
the derivative of the cofunction is recalled from the pattern of its partner without the sign
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives the derivative of cotangent or cosecant without the negative sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The result point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which rule applies to an expression written as one function over another, and have the student name the rule before computing.
errors.name: Trigonometric quotient differentiated term by term
non_conceptual_causes: the rewritten quotient is differentiated with the sum rule pattern from the line above
the numerator and the denominator are written on separate lines and are then processed independently
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the numerator and the denominator of a rewritten trigonometric quotient separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The rule point and the result point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two computed numbers is a slope and which is a height.
errors.name: Function value used as the slope of the tangent line
non_conceptual_causes: the function value and the derivative value are computed in one pass and the wrong one is placed in the slope position
the point of tangency is written first and its second coordinate is reused as the slope
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the tangent line using the value of the function at the point as its slope.
