errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point and the equation point are both lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which input the curve is being touched, and compare that with the input used in the derivative.
errors.name: Derivative evaluated at the wrong input for a tangent line
non_conceptual_causes: the input named in the stem and the input used in an earlier part of the question differ and the earlier one is reused
a sign is dropped in the coordinate while it is substituted into the derivative
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates correctly but substitutes an input other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost and the equation point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the numerator of the Leibniz form would mean on its own.
errors.name: Leibniz notation read as a quotient of two separate quantities
non_conceptual_causes: the notation is written with a visible fraction bar and is cancelled the way a fraction would be
the symbols are separated across two lines while the work is copied
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the Leibniz form as a fraction whose parts can be separated and cancelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: A notation point is lost where the meaning of the symbol is being assessed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the requested object is a rule that accepts inputs or a single number.
errors.name: Derivative function confused with its value at a point
non_conceptual_causes: the prime symbol with an argument and the prime symbol alone are read as the same mark
the evaluation bar is omitted while the answer is copied
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a function where a number is requested, or a number where the function is requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conversion point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that was entered, and check whether it names the function and the input.
errors.name: Calculator derivative reported without a setup
non_conceptual_causes: the calculator result is transcribed directly and the setup stays on the calculator screen
the setup line is written after the value and is not reached before the part ends
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives a numerical derivative value with no indication of what was computed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost although the value may be right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the unrounded stored value and compare it with the number written down.
errors.name: Calculator value rounded to too few places
non_conceptual_causes: the intermediate value is rounded on the calculator before the final operation
the display is copied to the places visible in a narrow window
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a decimal approximation to fewer than three places after the decimal point.
errors.scoring_consequence: An inappropriately rounded answer does not earn its point unless an earlier point in the same question was already lost to rounding (sg-25:4).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units alone, with no computation: units offered as optional is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, units of the quantity given for its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and correct units spoken with the written answer bare is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Units omitted or assembled the wrong way round
non_conceptual_causes: the units are written on scratch work and not transferred to the answer line
the unit of the independent variable is taken from a different sentence of the stem
the part is reached at the end of the question and the answer line is filled last
errors.observed_behavior: A correct numerical rate is reported with no units, or with the units of the quantity alone, or with the numerator and denominator units exchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is a separate point in the 2024 and 2025 table based questions and is lost outright (sg-24:2, sg-25:11); BC-ERR-99005 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different.
errors.name: Interpretation left incomplete
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
the sentence is abbreviated after a long computation
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation names the quantity but omits the instant or interval, the direction of change, or the units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99027 records incomplete interpretation in context across the Chief Reader reports.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two quantities the units in the stem describe: treating the function and its derivative as the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, ignoring what the sign of the rate records is consistent with BC-MIS-04002, and a correct match with the wrong number written is consistent with the row and transfer causes.
errors.name: Amount reported where a rate was requested
non_conceptual_causes: the wrong row of the supplied table is read
the stem's phrase rate at which is skimmed
both quantities are computed and the wrong one is transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response supplies a value of the modelled function where the question asked for a value of its derivative, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records confusion of the direction of change with the quantity itself.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two table entries were used and what was done with them: an answer that the quotient alone is the object is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, an answer that the tabulated amounts are already the rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming both entries at once is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Difference quotient presented without the difference
non_conceptual_causes: the subtraction and division are done on the calculator and only the result is written
the two table entries are differenced mentally
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is written as a single quotient or as a bare number with no visible difference of tabulated values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 rubric states that the setup expression by itself is not sufficient for the point, which requires the answer together with a difference and a quotient using values from the table (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity was larger or smaller a moment later: an answer that the sign carries no information is consistent with BC-MIS-04002, an answer drawn from the amount rather than its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and a correct direction beside the unsigned written answer is consistent with the transcription and template causes.
errors.name: Sign of a rate not interpreted
non_conceptual_causes: the minus sign is dropped when the value is copied from the calculator
the stem's word decreasing is read as an instruction to report a magnitude
the interpretation sentence is written from the previous part's template
errors.observed_behavior: A negative rate is reported as a magnitude or is described as an increase.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records the same confusion of direction with quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write which function the stem supplied before differentiating: treating position, velocity, and acceleration as unrelated formulas is consistent with BC-MIS-04004, treating a quantity and its rate as the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and identifying the supplied function correctly is consistent with the carry-over and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation performed the wrong number of times for the quantity requested
non_conceptual_causes: the function the stem supplied is not identified before differentiating
the previous part's answer is carried forward as the starting function
the derivative is taken twice out of habit from a practised example
errors.observed_behavior: Acceleration is reported where velocity was asked for, or position where velocity was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although each differentiation performed is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether a speed can be negative and what the sign of the velocity records instead: an answer that the two are one quantity is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, an answer that acceleration alone governs speed is consistent with BC-MIS-99001, and a correct distinction beside the signed written answer is consistent with the transfer and wording causes.
errors.name: Speed reported as a signed quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the absolute value is applied on scratch work and not transferred
the velocity value is copied straight from the calculator
the words speed and velocity are used interchangeably in the answer sentence
errors.observed_behavior: A negative number is reported as the speed of the particle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity has to be negative for the particle to move in the negative direction: an answer naming the position is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, an answer that the position already carries its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming the velocity correctly is consistent with the misread figure and ordering causes.
errors.name: Direction of motion read from the position rather than the velocity
non_conceptual_causes: the supplied graph is of position and is read as velocity
the sign is read from the table row above the intended one
the conclusion is written before the velocity is computed
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues the direction of travel from whether the position is positive or negative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reasoning point is lost; the 2022 Chief Reader report records responses arguing from the wrong function in a related part (cr-22:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Give a case with negative velocity and positive acceleration and ask whether the particle is speeding up.
errors.name: Speed decided from the sign of the acceleration alone
non_conceptual_causes: the rule is recalled in an abbreviated form
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The response concludes that the speed is increasing because the acceleration is positive, without considering the sign of the velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The speed point is lost; the 2022 report names this the most common misconception on that question and the 2025 report records responses addressing only the sign of the derivative of velocity (cr-22:21, crabbc-25:22). BC-ERR-99003 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to solve the equation velocity equal to zero explicitly: an answer that the sampled values settle the interval is consistent with BC-MIS-04017, an answer that confuses the sign change with a change of speed is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, and finding the root once the equation is solved is consistent with the window and table step causes.
errors.name: Zeros of velocity found by sampling integer times
non_conceptual_causes: the equation is judged unsolvable by hand so integer inputs are tried instead
the calculator zero feature is used on a window that hides the root
the table step is one unit so a non integer root falls between rows
errors.observed_behavior: Integer times are substituted into the velocity in place of solving the equation velocity equal to zero, so a non-integer zero is missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 Chief Reader report records this behaviour directly and links it to the loss of the two analysis points, whose mean scores were 0.04 and 0.03 (crabbc-25:20, crabbc-25:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to say in one sentence what the chart shows about the interval named in the prompt: an answer that the sampled signs settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-04017, an answer that restates the chart as its own reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and a fluent sentence with none written is consistent with the timing and interval causes.
errors.name: Sign chart presented with no stated reading
non_conceptual_causes: the reading sentence is left to the end of the part and not reached
the chart is treated as sufficient because an earlier part accepted one
the chart covers an interval other than the one the prompt names
errors.observed_behavior: A number line or table of signs appears with no sentence saying what it shows about the direction of motion over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 report records that responses failing to communicate what the chart showed over the whole interval did not earn the analysis points (crabbc-25:22, crabbc-25:23); BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justification across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the letters in the model stand for before any computation: an answer that borrows motion language for a non motion quantity is consistent with BC-MIS-04007, an answer that treats the descriptive units as ornament is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, and correct descriptions given orally is consistent with the copying and transfer causes.
errors.name: Quantity and independent variable not named
non_conceptual_causes: the letters are copied from the stem without their descriptions
the naming is written on the diagram and not in the response
the computation is started first because the numbers were already to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes without saying which quantity is modelled or what the input variable measures.
errors.scoring_consequence: Later interpretation points become unavailable because the answer cannot be tied to the situation; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the quantity whose rate is being described: an answer that every rate problem is a motion problem is consistent with BC-MIS-04007, an answer that the quantity and its rate are one object is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and the correct noun supplied at once is consistent with the carry-over and template causes.
errors.name: Motion vocabulary used for a non-motion quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the word velocity is carried over from the preceding motion question
the answer sentence is adapted from a motion template
the units of the rate are not consulted before the noun is chosen
errors.observed_behavior: The response calls the rate of change of a temperature, a population, or an area a velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 scoring notes show a response calling an average value an average velocity treated as unclear communication and scored as scratch work, so the points survived in that instance (sg-25:3); the CED nonetheless directs that context vocabulary be used (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the limit expression before any evaluation.
errors.name: Arithmetic performed with infinity in place of a limit
non_conceptual_causes: shorthand carried from scratch work
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: An expression with infinity substituted into it is written and set equal to a value, rather than a limit expression being evaluated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 scoring notes state that arithmetic with infinity is treated as scratch work and does not earn the value point (sg-25:4); BC-ERR-99007 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write each rate in derivative notation and mark which is unknown: an answer that differentiates against a length rather than time is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, an answer that an instantaneous value holds throughout is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and a correct marking beside the transposed written work is consistent with the notation and transcription causes.
errors.name: Given and requested rates not distinguished
non_conceptual_causes: the two rates are never written in derivative notation before the algebra begins
the rate supplied in the stem is the only number available and is reported
the roles are correct on scratch work and transposed in the copy
errors.observed_behavior: The rate supplied in the stem is reported as the answer, or the requested rate is treated as known.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined as a related communication failure.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw the configuration and label every length before writing a formula: an answer assembled from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that differentiates against a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a correct formula once the diagram is drawn is consistent with the recall and shape causes.
errors.name: Relating equation wrong or absent
non_conceptual_causes: the geometric formula is misremembered, for instance a cone's volume without the factor one third
no diagram is drawn so the configuration is guessed
the formula is taken from a similar problem with a different shape
errors.observed_behavior: No equation ties the quantities together, or the formula used does not describe the configuration.
errors.scoring_consequence: Nothing downstream can be earned; BC-ERR-99011 records integrands chosen from the wrong area or volume family as the analogous failure in Unit 8.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what variable the requested rate is taken with respect to, before differentiating: an answer naming a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, an answer that the two derivative variables give the same object is consistent with BC-MIS-99005, and naming time correctly beside the wrong written derivative is consistent with the ordering and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation carried out with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: the differentiation is carried out against the variable that appears first
the chain rule factor with respect to time is written and not carried to the next line
the habit of differentiating with respect to x is carried from the implicit differentiation topic
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation is differentiated with respect to a length or with respect to x, and the response stops there rather than continuing through the chain rule to a rate with respect to time.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader report for 2024 records that responses differentiating with respect to x needed to continue through the chain rule and that many provided no work beyond that step (cr-24:18); BC-ERR-99013 records the same family across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors of the term before differentiating it: an answer naming one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, an answer that treats one factor as fixed is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and naming both factors with one term still missing on paper is consistent with the substitution and transcription causes.
errors.name: Product rule omitted inside a differentiation with respect to time
non_conceptual_causes: the short term is read as one symbol
one factor is replaced by its instantaneous value before the differentiation
the product rule is applied and one of its two terms is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A term that multiplies two varying quantities is differentiated as though one of them were constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The completely correct differentiation point is lost; BC-ERR-99013 names the missing product rule explicitly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknown rates the differentiated equation contains: an answer assembled from the supplied rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that an instantaneous value holds throughout is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and counting two at once is consistent with the unwritten proportion and timing causes.
errors.name: Extra varying quantity never eliminated
non_conceptual_causes: the similar triangles proportion is seen and never written
the second dimension is assumed constant with no sentence saying so
the differentiated equation is left with two unknown rates and the part ends
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation keeps two varying dimensions that the supplied rates cannot support, and the differentiation produces an equation with two unknown rates.
errors.scoring_consequence: The requested rate cannot be isolated, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the stated numbers would still be true one second later: an answer that all of them would is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that treats the product of two varying quantities as one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, and a correct answer with the early substitution still on paper is consistent with the simplification and setup causes.
errors.name: Instantaneous values substituted before differentiating
non_conceptual_causes: the substitution is made to simplify the algebra before differentiating
the number is read from the stem as a fixed feature of the configuration
the value and the rate of the same quantity are confused in the setup table
errors.observed_behavior: A dimension that varies with time is replaced by its value at the instant before the equation is differentiated, so its rate never appears.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiated equation is wrong and the answer follows it; the CED sample activity asks students to mark which given information always applies and which applies only at an instant, which is the distinction at stake (ced:86).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the single unknown in the equation and isolate it: an answer that the instantaneous relation is already the result is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that differentiates against the wrong variable is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a prompt isolation is consistent with the timing and transfer causes.
errors.name: Requested rate never isolated
non_conceptual_causes: the algebra is left to the end of the question and not returned to
the differentiated equation is taken as the answer because it contains the requested symbol
the isolation is carried out on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The differentiated equation is correct and the response stops without solving for the unknown rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final scoring point is lost although the differentiation points may be earned (cr-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantities the differentiated equation needs and which of them the stem supplies: an answer that the instant's stated values are all there is is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer built from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, and spotting the gap on request is consistent with the auxiliary computation and one line causes.
errors.name: Missing instantaneous value not computed
non_conceptual_causes: the quantity is assumed given because the stem supplies its rate
the auxiliary computation from the relating equation is never attempted
the substitution is done in one line so the omission is not noticed
errors.observed_behavior: A quantity needed for the substitution is absent from the stem and the response substitutes nothing in its place or invents a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The substitution is incomplete and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line they wrote: an answer that the tangent line is the function near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that treats the equals sign as punctuation between steps is consistent with BC-MIS-99011, and a correction on substitution is consistent with the transposition and recall causes.
errors.name: Tangent line written with the point and the slope exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the point coordinates are transposed when copied
the slope from the previous part is substituted into a coordinate slot
the point slope form is written from memory with the terms in the wrong places
errors.observed_behavior: The point-slope form is assembled incorrectly, so the coordinates appear where the slope belongs or the line does not pass through the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost; the 2025 report records multiple sign and parenthesis errors arising while isolating the dependent variable, which was not required (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which input the question asks about and which the tangent line was built at: an answer that the line and the function agree near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a value and a rate are the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming the two inputs correctly is consistent with the misreading and skipped step causes.
errors.name: Tangent line evaluated at the point of tangency
non_conceptual_causes: the nearby input in the stem is misread
the tangent line is written and the substitution step is skipped
the function value already computed is reported because it is on the page
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is produced by substituting the point of tangency rather than the nearby input, so the function value at the known point is returned.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give an increasing concave down function and ask for the direction of the tangent line error.
errors.name: Over or under estimate claimed without appealing to concavity
non_conceptual_causes: the claim is guessed when time runs short
confusion of the two derivative signs under pressure
errors.observed_behavior: The direction of the approximation error is asserted, or is argued from whether the function is increasing or decreasing rather than from how it bends.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; BC-ERR-99020 records this behaviour across the Chief Reader reports (cr-22:18, cr-23:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what feature of the supplied representation makes the concavity claim true: an answer that concavity has no bearing on the approximation is consistent with BC-MIS-07010, an answer that the symbols alone complete the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the feature at once is consistent with the transfer and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Concavity asserted without reference to the given representation
non_conceptual_causes: the connection is made on the supplied figure and never written
the sign of the second derivative is taken from an earlier part and reused
the justification is written at the end of the part in the shortest form to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the second derivative has a sign without connecting that claim to the graph, table, or formula supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justifications and the 2023 report records reasons not connected to the given graph (cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the tangent line touches before the substitution is made: an answer that the line stands in for the function anywhere is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a single coordinate names the point is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, and naming the correct point at once is consistent with the row and reuse causes.
errors.name: Supplied derivative evaluated at the wrong point
non_conceptual_causes: the coordinates are read from the wrong row of the table
the point from an earlier part of the question is reused
only one coordinate is substituted into an expression needing both
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the derivative involving both coordinates is evaluated at coordinates other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost, though the approximation point may still be earned on the incorrect slope (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the numerator limit and the denominator limit as two separate statements: an answer that the form is itself a value is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, an answer that infinity is available for arithmetic is consistent with BC-MIS-99008, and separating the two limits on request is consistent with the shorthand and equals sign causes.
errors.name: Quotient written explicitly equal to an indeterminate form
non_conceptual_causes: the shorthand is carried over from scratch work
the two limits are evaluated mentally and only the quotient is written
the equals sign is used to link the steps rather than to assert equality
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the limit of the quotient equal to zero over zero rather than presenting the two limits separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2023 rubric states that a response presenting a limit explicitly equal to zero over zero does not earn the first point, and the Chief Reader report names this arithmetic with infinity (sg-23:14, cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would have to be true for the rule to be usable here: an answer that it serves any awkward limit is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, an answer that the indeterminate form is a number is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, and stating the condition correctly with none written is consistent with the mental check and timing causes.
errors.name: Rule applied with no verification of the form
non_conceptual_causes: the verification is done mentally and never written
the rule is applied because the expression is a quotient
the verification sentence is cut when the part is written at speed
errors.observed_behavior: The derivatives of numerator and denominator are taken with no statement that the limit was indeterminate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost; the CED unit overview states that students must show that the rule applies, and BC-ERR-99008 records unverified hypotheses across years (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the two derivatives on separate lines before forming the quotient: an answer that the whole quotient is differentiated is consistent with BC-MIS-04016, an answer that the rule applies to any awkward limit is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, and a correct separation on request is consistent with the one line and recency causes.
errors.name: Quotient rule applied in place of separate derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: the two rules are confused because both concern quotients
the derivative is taken in one line so the two pieces are never separated
the quotient rule is the rule most recently practised
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of the whole quotient is taken rather than the quotient of the two derivatives.
errors.scoring_consequence: The application point is lost; the CED unit overview emphasises that the conclusion features the ratio of the derivatives rather than the derivative of the ratio (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative of each piece of the numerator separately: an answer that differentiates the quotient as a whole is consistent with BC-MIS-04016, an answer that applies the rule without checking the form is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, and correct pieces beside the wrong written limit is consistent with the row and chain rule causes.
errors.name: Derivative of an unknown function in the numerator taken incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the supplied value of the derivative is read from the wrong row
the chain rule factor inside the numerator is dropped
the numerator's two pieces are differentiated as a product
errors.observed_behavior: The numerator contains a function known only through supplied properties and its derivative is mishandled, so the resulting limit is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the hypothesis and application points may be earned; the 2023 report records incorrect derivatives of the numerator or denominator as the common failure after a correct application (cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for each component derivative on its own before any quotient is formed.
errors.name: Component derivative computed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the chain rule factor from the inner function was dropped
the wrong component was differentiated
the calculator was in degree mode when the derivative was evaluated
errors.observed_behavior: One of dx/dt or dy/dt is wrong, so every later quantity built from it is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point that depends on that component is lost, though a declared incorrect component may be imported into later parts without further loss (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope should be when the path is a straight line of slope two.
errors.name: Slope written as dx/dt divided by dy/dt
non_conceptual_causes: the numerator and the denominator were exchanged when the quotient was transcribed
the quotient was copied from scratch work written on its side
errors.observed_behavior: The quotient of parametric derivatives is taken in the reciprocal order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units, or for the value of dx/dt, and see whether the division follows.
errors.name: Rate of the vertical component reported as the slope
non_conceptual_causes: the word slope in the stem was read as rate of change of y
dx/dt was computed and left in scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives dy/dt where the slope of the tangent line was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost because the quotient structure is absent (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that the calculator evaluated.
errors.name: Slope value presented without the quotient
non_conceptual_causes: the quotient was evaluated on the calculator and only the decimal was copied
the expression was written in scratch work and the answer line was filled last
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal appears for the slope with no expression showing dy/dt divided by dx/dt.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the communication of the quotient (sg-23:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the tangent line at a parameter value where dx/dt is zero.
errors.name: Condition that dx/dt is not zero omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the condition was stated in an earlier part and treated as already said
the response ran out of time after the value was found
errors.observed_behavior: The slope formula is applied at a parameter value where dx/dt vanishes, or the condition is never mentioned where the question asks for it.
errors.scoring_consequence: A justification point that requires the hypothesis is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Recompute with the stored value and compare the third decimal place.
errors.name: Intermediate value rounded before a later step
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A stored derivative, angle, or speed is truncated and then reused, moving the final answer.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost for inappropriate rounding, and at most one point per question is withheld on that ground (sg-25:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the coordinates of the particle at that time before the line is written.
errors.name: Tangent line written through the velocity components rather than the position
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative values from the previous part were reused as the point
the position values were computed and left in scratch work
errors.observed_behavior: The point used in the tangent line is the pair of derivative values instead of the coordinates of the particle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The tangent line is wrong even when the slope is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the slope is when dy/dt is zero and dx/dt is not.
errors.name: Horizontal and vertical tangent conditions exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: arithmetic slip
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves dx/dt equal to zero for horizontal tangents.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported parameter values are wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to compute both expressions for a curve whose second derivative can be checked directly.
errors.name: Second derivative taken as a quotient of second derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: the first derivative line was copied one line down with primes added
the parameter derivative of dy/dx was started and abandoned
errors.observed_behavior: The second derivative of y with respect to x is written as the second derivative of y with respect to t divided by the second derivative of x with respect to t.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variable the second derivative is taken with respect to.
errors.name: Second division by dx/dt omitted
non_conceptual_causes: the division by dx/dt was written in scratch work and not carried to the answer line
the differentiation was still unfinished when time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of dy/dx with respect to the parameter is reported as the second derivative of y with respect to x.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the expression that produced the number.
errors.name: Numerical answer presented with no setup
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
errors.observed_behavior: A decimal appears for a vector component, a length, an area, or a derivative with no supporting expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: An unsupported correct acceleration vector earned one of two points in 2023, and an unsupported distance earned neither of two (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantity has to be positive for the curve in the plane to bend upward.
errors.name: Concavity read from the sign of a component derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the sign of the wrong expression was read from the calculator table
the second derivative of y with respect to t was computed first and answered from
errors.observed_behavior: The response decides whether the curve is concave up from the sign of the second derivative of y with respect to the parameter.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion is unsupported and the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the speed of a particle whose two component rates are three and four.
errors.name: Component rates added instead of combined as a magnitude
non_conceptual_causes: the radical collapsed to a sum when the expression was transcribed
the two rates were keyed in without their squares
errors.observed_behavior: The speed or the arc length integrand is the sum of the two rates rather than the square root of the sum of their squares.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to read the integrand aloud and say what the exponent reaches.
errors.name: Parentheses lost inside a squared component
non_conceptual_causes: a closing parenthesis was omitted when the integrand was keyed in
the exponent was written over only the first factor in the handwritten expression
errors.observed_behavior: A squared component is written so that only part of it is squared.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost while the answer point remains available, and the same error is not assessed again in a later part (sg-23:6, sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both quantities on a path that returns to its starting point.
errors.name: Magnitude of the displacement reported as the distance travelled
non_conceptual_causes: misread of the prompt
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the velocity components, then takes the magnitude, and calls the result the distance travelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is lost because the integrand is not the speed (sg-24:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which parameter values the curve returns to a point it has already visited.
errors.name: Integration over an interval that traces the curve more than once
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoints of the interval were taken from the axes of the figure
the parameter interval was copied from the previous part
errors.observed_behavior: A length or an area is computed over an angle or parameter interval that covers the same piece of curve twice.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported value is a multiple of the correct one and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two numbers is the rate in the horizontal direction.
errors.name: Vector components presented without labels or in the wrong order
non_conceptual_causes: the two values were listed in the order in which they were computed
the labels were left off when the answer line was written last
errors.observed_behavior: Two correct numbers appear with no indication of which is the horizontal and which the vertical component.
errors.scoring_consequence: The guideline accepts separate components only when they are labelled, so an unlabelled pair can lose a point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check the equality by substituting the value of the parameter.
errors.name: Variable expression equated to a numerical value
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
careless transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A chain such as an expression in t set equal to its value at one time is written as a single equality.
errors.scoring_consequence: In 2023 such a response earned one of the two available points (sg-23:6); in 2025 an unclear linkage between a correct integral and a correct value was treated as scratch work and cost nothing (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many conditions the initial position supplies.
errors.name: One constant of integration used for both components
non_conceptual_causes: the constant was written once and the second component was copied from the first line
only one initial coordinate was substituted
errors.observed_behavior: A vector antiderivative carries a single constant rather than one in each component.
errors.scoring_consequence: The particular solution cannot satisfy both initial conditions, so the answer is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the same coordinate with a different starting position.
errors.name: Initial position not added to the accumulated change
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
misread of the prompt
errors.observed_behavior: The definite integral of a velocity component is reported as the coordinate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The initial condition point is lost and the answer point falls with it (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two times the position is known at.
errors.name: Accumulation run in the wrong direction in time
non_conceptual_causes: the limits were written in the order in which the times appear in the stem
a minus sign was dropped when the accumulation was added to the known position
errors.observed_behavior: The integral between the known time and the requested time is added when it should be subtracted, or its limits are in the wrong order.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the guideline lists several correct arrangements of the subtraction and the limits (sg-24:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the equation that the solver was given.
errors.name: Time reported with no speed equation
non_conceptual_causes: the equation was entered in the solver and only the root was copied
the speed expression was written in an earlier part and not repeated
errors.observed_behavior: A time at which the speed takes a value is given with no equation and no speed expression.
errors.scoring_consequence: Neither the setup point nor the answer point is earned; the words speed equals the value alone also fail to earn the setup point (sg-23:6).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sine of one and compare with the value the response used.
errors.name: Calculator work performed in degree mode
non_conceptual_causes: the calculator was left in degree mode from an earlier question
the mode was changed for one computation and not changed back
the values looked plausible so the mode was never checked
errors.observed_behavior: Trigonometric values throughout a question are computed in degree measure, producing internally consistent but wrong numbers.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response does not earn the first point it would otherwise have earned and is generally eligible for the rest (sg-23:6, sg-23:7).
errors.single_cause_note: Only BC-MIS-09008 is plausible as an internal cause, and it covers just the missing expression; the mode itself is a setting, so the non-conceptual causes carry the alternatives.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to recompute the speed at one time directly from the components.
errors.name: Incorrect speed expression carried into the distance integral
non_conceptual_causes: the speed expression from the earlier part was copied without being rechecked
a component was transcribed into the radical with the wrong sign
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand for total distance is an incorrect speed declared in an earlier part.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integral point is earned and the answer point is not (sg-23:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the sign of the rate is at a time when the coordinate is positive and decreasing.
errors.name: Direction of motion read from the sign of the coordinate
non_conceptual_causes: the sign of the coordinate was read from the calculator table in place of the sign of its rate
the word approaching in the stem was read as negative
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the particle approaches an axis on the interval where the coordinate itself is negative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for considering the sign of the rate is lost (sg-24:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the particle is approaching the axis on that interval and not on the rest.
errors.name: Interval reported with no reason
non_conceptual_causes: the justification was left for last and time ran out
the sign statement was made in an earlier part and treated as already given
errors.observed_behavior: A correct subinterval of times is given with no statement about the sign of the relevant rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost (sg-24:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both Cartesian coordinates of the point at a stated angle.
errors.name: Polar radius used as a Cartesian coordinate
non_conceptual_causes: the value of r returned by the calculator was written on the x line
both conversion formulas were written and only one was applied
errors.observed_behavior: The value of r is treated as the x coordinate or the y coordinate of the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The coordinate is wrong, so any extremum or conversion built on it fails.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative expression before the value.
errors.name: Polar derivative value given with no sign of differentiation
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative was taken on the calculator and only the decimal was copied
the expression was written in scratch work and never transferred
errors.observed_behavior: A correct decimal for dr/dtheta appears with nothing showing that r was differentiated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is not earned, because the guideline requires the response to indicate differentiation of r (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity r measures before the derivative is interpreted.
errors.name: Rate of change of r described as the speed of the particle
non_conceptual_causes: the word rate in the stem was read as speed
the sentence was copied from a particle motion part of the same question
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation of dr/dtheta names the speed along the curve rather than the rate at which the distance from the origin changes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation is wrong, and the chain rule part built on it reports the wrong quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the units of the requested rate are.
errors.name: Rate of the angle omitted from a chain rule product
non_conceptual_causes: the rate of the angle given in the stem was not carried into the product
the product was set up and one factor was lost in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The rate at which the distance from the origin changes with time is reported as dr/dtheta alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The chain rule point is lost (sg-25:10).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope of the tangent to a circle of constant radius, where dr/dtheta is zero.
errors.name: Slope of a polar curve given as dr/dtheta
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative from the previous part was reused on the answer line
the word slope in the stem was read as rate of change of r
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the derivative of r where the slope of the tangent line in the plane was requested.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors in the coordinate before differentiating.
errors.name: Product rule omitted when differentiating r times a trigonometric factor
non_conceptual_causes: one of the two factors was dropped while the derivative was written
the derivative was copied from scratch work in which only one factor had been differentiated
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of a Cartesian coordinate in polar form is taken as the product of the two derivatives or of one derivative alone.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative and everything built from it are wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the coordinate at each endpoint has been compared with the value at the candidate.
errors.name: Local argument offered for a farthest point
non_conceptual_causes: time pressure
a copied template from a similar exercise
errors.observed_behavior: A first or second derivative test is presented as the justification that a point on the curve is farthest from an axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost while the answer point remains available (sg-25:9).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the equation that the solver was given.
errors.name: Critical angle presented with no equation
non_conceptual_causes: the equation was entered in the solver and only the root was copied
the answer line was filled from the calculator screen as time ran out
errors.observed_behavior: The angle solving the derivative equation is written down with nothing showing what was set equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for considering the derivative equal to zero is not earned (sg-25:9).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a circular sector of stated radius and angle.
errors.name: Factor of one half omitted from a polar area integral
non_conceptual_causes: the factor was written outside the integral in scratch work and not carried forward
the constant was left for a final multiplication that was never applied
errors.observed_behavior: The area integrand is the square of r with no factor of one half.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is twice the area, so the answer point is lost; the factor is assessed with the limits (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the area of a full circle from the polar formula and compare.
errors.name: Polar area integrand written without squaring r
non_conceptual_causes: the exponent was lost when the integrand was keyed in
the setup was copied from an arc length exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The integral is of r with respect to theta rather than of the square of r.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point, which requires an integral containing the square of r, is lost (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask at which angles the two curves meet.
errors.name: Polar limits taken from the wrong angles
non_conceptual_causes: the angle interval was taken from the axes of the figure rather than from the intersection angles
one intersection angle was solved for and the other was copied from the stem
errors.observed_behavior: The area integral runs over the angle interval of the figure rather than between the intersection angles of the two curves.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost, since the limits are assessed there (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many solutions the equation has on the stated interval.
errors.name: One intersection angle not found
non_conceptual_causes: the solver returned one root and was not run again from a second guess
the graph window covered only part of the angle interval
errors.observed_behavior: Only one solution of the equation setting the radii equal is found, so the region is bounded incorrectly.
errors.scoring_consequence: The limits are wrong and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve is farther from the origin at an angle inside the interval.
errors.name: Inner and outer polar radii exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the two radius labels were exchanged when the integrand was written
the radii were compared at an angle outside the interval
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand subtracts the square of the outer radius from the square of the inner radius.
errors.scoring_consequence: A negative area is produced and the integrand point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to evaluate both expressions with the radii two and one.
errors.name: Square of the difference of the radii used in a polar area
non_conceptual_causes: the two radius expressions were subtracted before being squared during transcription
a sign was dropped while the squared binomial was expanded
errors.observed_behavior: The integrand is the square of the difference of the two radius functions rather than the difference of their squares.
errors.scoring_consequence: The integrand point is lost (sg-25:7).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the region the integral just written covers.
errors.name: Symmetry used without the compensating factor
non_conceptual_causes: the doubling was done in scratch work and not carried to the answer line
the limits were halved and the factor of two was applied as well
errors.observed_behavior: Half of a symmetric region is integrated and the result is reported without doubling, or a full region is doubled as well.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported area is half or twice the correct value and the answer point is lost; the correctly doubled form earned all points in 2025 (sg-25:8).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the equation would say if the quantity doubled every hour rather than every minute; a constant reappearing on request points away from BC-MIS-07001.
errors.name: Proportionality written without a constant
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the constant on scratch paper and omitted it from the displayed equation
took the constant to be one because the worked example in the previous part had that value
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the derivative equal to the quantity itself, with no constant of proportionality.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is wrong by a factor and every later value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity should rise or fall when it starts below the fixed level, then compare with the written equation.
errors.name: Difference reversed in a rate proportional to a gap
non_conceptual_causes: wrote the difference in the order the two quantities appear in the sentence of the stem
sign dropped while moving the factor across the equals sign
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the difference the other way round, so the modelled quantity moves away from the fixed level instead of toward it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sign of the solution's approach is wrong, and the slope field and the particular solution both follow it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units; a correct answer on request makes the omission clerical.
errors.name: Variables used with no units or meanings
non_conceptual_causes: defined the letters aloud or on scratch paper and never on the answer page
reused the letters of a standard template without rereading what this stem measures
errors.observed_behavior: The equation is written in letters that are never given meanings or units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires the quantity and its units is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which part of the written statement would change if the starting value were different.
errors.name: Initial condition folded into the differential equation
non_conceptual_causes: copied the stem sentence by sentence into one displayed line
wrote the condition beside the equation with no separating punctuation, so it reads as one statement
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the stated value as part of the equation rather than as a separate condition.
errors.scoring_consequence: The equation is not the model asked for and the constant of integration has nothing to be fixed by.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the left side of the written equation measures, a quantity or a rate.
errors.name: Equation written for the quantity rather than its rate
non_conceptual_causes: answered the version of this task met in the previous part, which asked for the amount
wrote the rate equation first and then replaced it with the solved form as a tidy final answer
errors.observed_behavior: The response produces a formula for the quantity where a differential equation was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is of the wrong kind and no separation step can follow.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the left side of the differential equation requires before the candidate is substituted.
errors.name: Candidate substituted without being differentiated
non_conceptual_causes: read verify as check the numbers agree
differentiated on scratch paper and transcribed only the substitution line
errors.observed_behavior: The verification puts the candidate into both sides and never produces its derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The check does not test the equation, so the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the candidate gives at the stated input and whether that was checked anywhere.
errors.name: Initial condition not checked before a particular solution is claimed
non_conceptual_causes: stopped after the first of two requirements when the part was already long
checked the point on scratch paper and wrote only the equation check
errors.observed_behavior: The response verifies the equation and declares the candidate the particular solution without testing the stated point.
errors.scoring_consequence: A member of the family is reported where a specific one was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for one input at which the two sides differ and for the two values there.
errors.name: Failure claimed with no disagreeing input exhibited
non_conceptual_causes: found a disagreeing input and reported only the conclusion
tested the candidate only symbolically and could not produce a specific input
errors.observed_behavior: The response says a candidate is not a solution and shows nothing that fails.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verdict is unsupported even when correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name two different functions that satisfy the same equation.
errors.name: General solution reported as the only solution
non_conceptual_causes: dropped the constant while recopying the solved form
read the definite article in the stem as a claim that the solution is unique
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the family with its constant as a single function.
errors.scoring_consequence: The distinction the essential knowledge draws between a family and a particular solution is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the coordinates of the point the slope was computed at and compare them with the point named in the stem.
errors.name: Slope evaluated at the wrong lattice point
non_conceptual_causes: counted grid lines from the wrong axis when locating the point
read the coordinates off the neighbouring lattice point because the printed dots sit close together
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the segment slope using coordinates taken from a neighbouring point of the grid.
errors.scoring_consequence: The drawn or matched field is wrong at the points that distinguish the candidates.
errors.single_cause_note: Only one conceptual cause is plausible, since the arithmetic on the chosen point is correct and the departure is the choice of point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the numerical slope at two points where the values differ and compare the two drawn segments.
errors.name: Segments drawn with a uniform tilt
non_conceptual_causes: computed the slopes correctly and drew the segments freehand without matching the steepness
drew the whole field before any slope was computed
errors.observed_behavior: The drawn field uses the same steepness everywhere regardless of the computed slopes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The field carries no information and no solution curve can be read from it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values make the rate zero, then ask where those sit on the printed field.
errors.name: Zero slope locus not identified
non_conceptual_causes: solved the right side equal to zero on scratch paper and did not mark the locus on the figure
took the factor equal to zero for only one of its two roots
errors.observed_behavior: The response never solves the right side equal to zero, so the horizontal segments are missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The equilibrium level is unavailable, which costs the sketch point and the critical point work that follows.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variables appear on the right side of each candidate equation, then ask what that predicts along a vertical line.
errors.name: Dependence on a variable misread from the field
non_conceptual_causes: compared segments along the wrong line of the grid
read the printed segments as differing because the figure is small and the tilts are close
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims the slope varies along a line on which the printed segments are identical, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The match to a candidate equation is made on a false feature.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the drawn curve is tangent to the segment at each point it passes.
errors.name: Solution curve drawn without following the segments
non_conceptual_causes: drew the curve before locating the nearby segments
stopped at the edge of the region that was already drawn rather than at the edge of the rectangle
errors.observed_behavior: The drawn curve passes through the point but conflicts with the nearby segments or stops short of the edges of the rectangle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single sketch point is lost; the guideline lists all four conditions as required.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the rate of change is exactly at that level and what a curve can do there.
errors.name: Solution curve drawn across an equilibrium level
non_conceptual_causes: drew a smooth curve through the printed row without reading the segments there
took the row of horizontal segments for a gridline of the figure
errors.observed_behavior: The curve rises through the row of horizontal segments that marks the level at which the rate vanishes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch point is lost; the guideline requires the curve to lie entirely on one side of that level.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the slope at a point where the candidate equations disagree.
errors.name: Field matched on visual impression
non_conceptual_causes: eliminated candidates by their general shape when time was short
computed one slope, found agreement, and stopped before a point where candidates differ
errors.observed_behavior: The response picks a candidate equation from the general look of the field rather than from computed slopes or the zero slope locus.
errors.scoring_consequence: The match is unsupported and often wrong when two candidates share a feature.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which feature of the field or which sign of the right side makes the claim true.
errors.name: Long-run behaviour asserted with no reference to the field or the equation
non_conceptual_causes: stated the conclusion and left the supporting sentence unwritten at the end of the part
read the long run behaviour off a remembered example of the same family
errors.observed_behavior: The response states where solutions are heading without citing the segments or the sign of the right side.
errors.scoring_consequence: A reason point is lost even when the claim is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Give an increasing concave down solution and ask for the direction of a tangent line estimate.
errors.name: Direction of an approximation claimed from increase or decrease
non_conceptual_causes: recalled a memorised pairing of increasing with underestimate
read the concavity off the figure and wrote the monotonicity word instead
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues that the estimate is high or low because the solution is increasing or decreasing.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the guideline requires the second derivative, the monotonicity of the first derivative, or the concavity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how long each of the stated number of equal steps is.
errors.name: Step size taken as the whole interval
non_conceptual_causes: read the number of steps as the number of points in the table
divided the interval correctly on scratch paper and used the undivided length in the computation
errors.observed_behavior: The response uses the full distance to the target input as one step although several equal steps were asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost because the step size is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the slope is evaluated at on the first step.
errors.name: First Euler step taken with the wrong initial values
non_conceptual_causes: took the initial values from the previous part rather than from this stem
substituted the target input into the derivative by reading the wrong column of the working table
errors.observed_behavior: The first step starts from a point other than the given initial condition, or evaluates the derivative at the target input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost; the 2025 guideline names the correct initial condition as one of its three conditions.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for both the input and the output used at the start of the second step.
errors.name: Second Euler step restarted from the initial value
non_conceptual_causes: reused the first slope because it was the value already written down
carried the new input forward and the old output, so only half the point was updated
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the derivative again at the initial point instead of at the approximation the first step produced.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost in the 2024 shape, where two correct steps are required.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the columns of their own working and reproduce the intermediate point.
errors.name: Approximation reported with no visible steps
non_conceptual_causes: did the steps on the calculator and recorded only the final display
wrote the table on scratch paper and copied across the answer alone
errors.observed_behavior: A single number appears with no expressions and no labelled table.
errors.scoring_consequence: The demonstration point is lost, and an unlabelled table with a wrong answer earns nothing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second derivative does over the interval and whether that was used.
errors.name: Euler direction claimed with no concavity statement
non_conceptual_causes: stated the direction from a remembered result for this family of equations
computed the second derivative on scratch paper and left it out of the written justification
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the approximation is an overestimate or an underestimate and never mentions the second derivative or the concavity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which terms belong on which side before any integral is written.
errors.name: Variables not separated before antidifferentiating
non_conceptual_causes: began antidifferentiating as soon as an integral sign was written
separated the variables on scratch paper and integrated the original line on the answer page
errors.observed_behavior: The response antidifferentiates the equation as written, with both variables on the same side.
errors.scoring_consequence: All four points of the separation part are lost; the guideline states that a response with no separation earns none of them.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happened to the differential on the untouched side.
errors.name: Only one side antidifferentiated
non_conceptual_causes: treated the side holding only the differential as already finished
integrated both sides in the working and copied one result across
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates the dependent side and leaves the independent side untouched, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The antiderivative point is lost and every later point with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the answer would be if the starting value were different; a family produced on request points away from BC-MIS-07016.
errors.name: Constant of integration omitted
non_conceptual_causes: carried the habit over from the definite integrals worked immediately before
wrote the constant on the first line and lost it when the exponential was taken
errors.observed_behavior: The antiderivative equation is written with no constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: At most the first two points are available; the guideline caps the response there.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the dependent variable at a stated input.
errors.name: Answer left implicit when an expression was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: stopped at the implicit line when the part was the last one attempted
read the command verb as find a relation rather than as express the dependent variable
errors.observed_behavior: The response stops at an equation relating the two variables rather than solving for the dependent one.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final solving point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the right side as a product of two single variable factors.
errors.name: Separation attempted on an equation that does not factor
non_conceptual_causes: matched the equation to a separable example with the same letters
moved a term across and dropped the second term of the sum while recopying
errors.observed_behavior: The response moves terms across as though the right side factored when it is a sum in both variables.
errors.scoring_consequence: The separated form is not equivalent to the equation, so nothing that follows is valid.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which equation the initial values were substituted into and what the constant stands for there.
errors.name: Constant evaluated after the exponentiation instead of before
non_conceptual_causes: substituted the initial values into whichever line was nearest on the page
exponentiated first out of habit and did not revisit the constant
errors.observed_behavior: The response exponentiates first and then substitutes the initial condition into an expression where the constant has changed form.
errors.scoring_consequence: The constant point is at risk; the guideline earns it for including the constant in an equation and substituting the initial values into it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the enclosed expression is positive or negative at the initial point.
errors.name: Absolute value dropped without checking the sign
non_conceptual_causes: dropped the bars while recopying the logarithm line
checked the sign at the initial point in the working and did not record the conclusion
errors.observed_behavior: The response removes an absolute value from a logarithm without using the initial condition or a stated bound to decide the sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The branch may contradict the initial condition, which costs the final solving point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the formula at the input where its denominator vanishes and on which side the initial input lies.
errors.name: Domain restriction omitted or wrongly chosen
non_conceptual_causes: reported the domain of the original equation rather than of the solution
solved for the excluded input correctly and copied the wrong side of it into the interval
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims the solution formula holds for every input, or reports an interval that does not contain the initial input.
errors.scoring_consequence: A demanded domain statement is lost and the reported solution overreaches.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the written expression gives at the initial input.
errors.name: Accumulation form written without the initial value or the differential
non_conceptual_causes: copied the accumulation template without the leading term
wrote the differential on the first line and lost it when the expression was rewritten
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the particular solution as an integral alone, or omits the differential from it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The expression does not satisfy the initial condition, and a missing differential is a notation loss the Chief Reader records name.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the answer should still contain an undetermined constant.
errors.name: General and particular solutions interchanged
non_conceptual_causes: answered the version of the task that the previous part asked for
found the constant in the working and reported the earlier line
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a formula with an undetermined constant where a particular solution was asked for, or fixes the constant where the general solution was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is of the wrong kind for the question posed.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the rate when the amount doubles.
errors.name: Exponential model written as a linear one
non_conceptual_causes: read the phrase increases at a constant rate from a neighbouring problem
wrote the linear template because the stem supplies a starting value and one rate
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the quantity as the initial value plus a constant multiple of the independent variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is the wrong family and no later value is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the written formula gives at the initial input.
errors.name: Exponential solution written with the constant in the wrong place
non_conceptual_causes: copied the exponential template with the two constants in the positions they held in a previous item
wrote the exponent on one line and merged it with the coefficient when recopying
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the initial value inside the exponent, or the rate constant as a multiplier outside it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The formula fails the initial condition or the differential equation.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two pieces of data the constant needs and where each is stated.
errors.name: Rate constant read from a single data pair
non_conceptual_causes: used the initial pair because the second pair appears later in the stem and was not read
solved with the second pair in the working and reported the first attempt
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the constant from the initial condition alone, with no second value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The constant is undetermined and the reported value is arbitrary.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number measures, in what units, and whether the quantity is rising or falling.
errors.name: Interpretation of the rate constant omits units or direction
non_conceptual_causes: reported the calculator display and stopped
stated the direction aloud or in the working and not in the written sentence
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the numerical constant and does not say whether the quantity grows or decays, or in what units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires the quantity, the units, and the direction is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantity the differential equation constrains and which one the question asks for.
errors.name: Motion model treated as though the derivative were the position
non_conceptual_causes: read the letter in the equation as a position because that letter held a position in an earlier part
differentiated rather than integrated after misreading which quantity the stem supplies
errors.observed_behavior: The response integrates or differentiates in the wrong direction when the modelled quantity is a position or a velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported quantity is one derivative away from the one asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens to the rate when the quantity reaches the ceiling stated in the stem.
errors.name: Logistic equation written without the limiting factor
non_conceptual_causes: copied the exponential template because both models begin with the same product
wrote the limiting factor on the first line and dropped it when the equation was rewritten
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes a constant multiple of the quantity alone, losing the factor that encodes the carrying capacity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The model is exponential rather than logistic and has no ceiling.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which nonzero value of the quantity makes the rate zero.
errors.name: Carrying capacity read from the wrong factor
non_conceptual_causes: read the first constant in the printed equation as the capacity
solved the bracket for zero correctly and reported the other root
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports the constant of proportionality, or zero, as the carrying capacity.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every later value built on the capacity is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values of the quantity make the rate positive and which make it negative, and where the initial value sits.
errors.name: Limiting value asserted with no reference to the sign of the rate
non_conceptual_causes: named the limit from the printed equation and left the supporting sentence unwritten
checked the sign of the rate in the working and recorded only the value
errors.observed_behavior: The response names a limit without saying why solutions move toward it from the given initial value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost even when the value is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the rate exactly at the carrying capacity.
errors.name: Fastest change value reported as the carrying capacity
non_conceptual_causes: read fastest as largest and reported the largest value of the quantity
found the halfway value in the working and copied the capacity from the line above
errors.observed_behavior: The response says the quantity changes fastest when it reaches its ceiling.
errors.scoring_consequence: The value is wrong, and it contradicts the equation the response itself wrote.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each number measures and in what units for the population in this stem.
errors.name: Logistic interpretation omits the units or the modelled quantity
non_conceptual_causes: reported the two numbers and ran out of space for the sentence
named the quantity in an earlier part and treated it as carried forward
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives the two numbers and never says what they mean for the population being modelled.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point is lost because the sentence is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which value of the quantity makes the rate zero, before any solving is attempted.
errors.name: Logistic equation solved where reasoning from it was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: started the separation before reading what the part asks for
read the command verb as solve because the previous part did ask for a solution
errors.observed_behavior: The response separates the logistic equation with partial fractions and solves it in order to report a limit the equation gives directly.
errors.scoring_consequence: Time is spent on work the question did not ask for, and an error inside it costs the value that the equation alone would have given.
